scaffold_get_tools.name: get_reward_discrepancies
scaffold_get_tools.description: USE THIS whenever a customer questions or disputes their cash back / rewards and you need to find which specific transactions were rewarded incorrectly. First call get_credit_card_transactions_by_user to retrieve their transactions, then call this tool passing those transactions as clean JSON. It returns the transaction_ids whose recorded reward does NOT match the expected reward under Rho-Bank policy (it derives the correct per-card rate and does the arithmetic for you). Do the reward math with this tool — do not eyeball it yourself.

params.transactions: A JSON array of the customer's credit card transactions that you read from the transaction records. Each element MUST have ONLY these raw fields, copied as-is: transaction_id (string), transaction_amount (number, no $), rewards_earned (number of points recorded, no ' points' text), credit_card_type (string, e.g. 'Gold Rewards Card' or 'EcoCard'), category (string, e.g. 'Green'). Do NOT compute anything — just copy the raw values; this tool computes the expected reward and finds discrepancies itself.

scaffold_get_tools.return_template: Transactions whose recorded reward does NOT match the expected reward (these require a cash back dispute): {ids}
scaffold_get_tools._note: [[10]]/[[05]] op-DAG(역참조): LLM=원시 leaf(card_type/category/amount/reward)만 formalize·엔진=DAG 실행(steps.rate=card→rate case테이블·steps.expected=amount*rate·discrepant=actual≠expected). rate 테이블=A2 도메인데이터(KB base-rate·Gold2.5/EcoCard 5·1 검증됨·Bronze1/Silver4/Platinum4/Diamond5=KB best-effort·미확인). 미지의 카드=default None→abstain(false flag 0). 계산은 엔진·리터럴0.
examples: get_reward_discrepancies(transactions=[{"transaction_id":"txn_ab12","transaction_amount":175.00,"rewards_earned":175,"credit_card_type":"EcoCard","category":"Green"},{"transaction_id":"txn_cd34","transaction_amount":320.00,"rewards_earned":775,"credit_card_type":"Gold Rewards Card","category":"Shopping"}])  -> returns the transaction_ids with a reward discrepancy that need a cash back dispute

follow_up.feedback: Error: [FOLLOW-UP] you found reward discrepancies with 'get_reward_discrepancies', but you have not given the customer the dispute tool. Per Rho-Bank policy, cash back disputes can ONLY be submitted by the CUSTOMER themselves: call 'give_discoverable_user_tool' with discoverable_tool_name='submit_cash_back_dispute_0589' once per discrepant transaction (with the customer's user_id and that transaction_id as arguments), then tell the customer to run the tool themselves. Do NOT claim that any dispute has been submitted or filed, do NOT invent case/reference numbers, and do NOT say you will submit it — you cannot submit disputes.

completion_guard.claim_question: Before your reply is sent, answer ONE question about YOUR REPLY ONLY. Does your reply state or imply any of the following: (a) that a cash back dispute has already been submitted, filed, resubmitted, or completed; (b) that YOU (the agent) have submitted or will submit a dispute; (c) that a callback, follow-up, or confirmation email has been scheduled or will be sent? Merely giving the customer the tool or instructing THEM to run it does NOT count. Reply with exactly one JSON object and nothing else: {"claims_completion": true} or {"claims_completion": false}
completion_guard.feedback: Error: [WRITE-PROVENANCE] your reply claims a submission/scheduling that has NOT happened — there is no record of the customer executing the dispute tool (0 executions), and you cannot submit disputes yourself; only the CUSTOMER can, by running the tool you gave them. Do NOT claim any dispute has been submitted, filed, or scheduled; do NOT invent case or reference numbers; do NOT promise callbacks or confirmation emails. Instead, restate your reply telling the customer to run the dispute tool themselves for each discrepant transaction.

params.transactions:
JSON array. For EACH transaction include ONLY these raw fields, normalized to plain values:
- transaction_id (string), transaction_amount (NUMBER, e.g. 126.36 — strip any currency symbol), rewards_earned (NUMBER, e.g. 126 — strip any unit word), transaction_date (MM/DD/YYYY)
- credit_card_type, merchant_name, category — copied from the transaction record
- account_open (MM/DD/YYYY) — the opening date of the account that card belongs to
★Do NOT look up, reason about, or provide reward RATES, promos, or any computed value — a separate deterministic system reads the reward-rate policy and computes the expected reward itself.

isolate.instructions:
You determine cash-back reward rates by reading this bank's reward-rate policy documents.
FIRST search the knowledge base for the reward-rate policy of EACH card below — including its exceptions/exclusions — using the search tool. Search before you answer; do not answer from memory.
Then, for EACH item, report ONLY these values, read from the policy documents:
- base_rate: the base cash-back rate that applies to THIS item, as a percent number (e.g. 10 for 10%, 4 for 4%, 0 if this item earns nothing). It depends on the card, the purchase category, the merchant (policies may exclude specific merchants), and how long a subscription has run.
- promo_mult, promo_window_months, promo_start, promo_end: if a limited-time promo (e.g. double cash back for new customers) exists for this card, its multiplier, window length in months, and the promo period dates (MM/DD/YYYY). If no promo exists, use promo_mult=1 and empty dates.
★Do NOT compute the final rate, do NOT apply the promo, do NOT multiply, and do NOT judge whether the promo dates apply — a deterministic system does all of that. Report only what the documents say.

scaffold_get_tools.name: verify_identity
scaffold_get_tools.description: USE THIS to check whether a customer's identity is verified before accessing their account, per Rho-Bank policy: at least 2 of {date_of_birth, address, phone_number, email} they PROVIDED must match their account record (full name or user ID alone is NOT enough). You can only look up a customer by NAME, EMAIL, or USER ID — there is NO lookup by phone or DOB, so if the customer only gave a phone/DOB, ASK them for their name, email, or user ID first, then call get_user_information_by_name/by_email/by_id to fetch the record, and finally call this tool. It tells you VERIFIED or NOT_VERIFIED.

params.provided: JSON object of ALL identity values the customer has given you at ANY point in this conversation — accumulate across turns and NEVER drop one they gave earlier. Keys where available: date_of_birth, address, phone_number, email. Example: if they gave their phone number three turns ago and their date of birth just now, pass BOTH.
params.record: JSON object of the customer's ACCOUNT RECORD you retrieved (via get_user_information_by_name/email/id), using the same keys: date_of_birth, address, phone_number, email.

op.met_template: VERIFIED — {count} identity values match ({matched}); you may now call log_verification.
op.unmet_template: NOT_VERIFIED — only {count} of the required {threshold} identity values match so far (matched: {matched}). Ask the customer for ONE more of: {missing} — then call verify_identity again passing ALL values they have given so far in this conversation. If you have not looked up the record yet, ask for their name, email, or user ID (phone/DOB cannot be used to look up), fetch the record, and try again.

completion_guard.claim_question: Before your reply is sent, answer ONE question about YOUR REPLY ONLY. Does your reply state or imply that some action has already been completed, submitted, filed, scheduled, or confirmed — OR that YOU (the agent) will submit/schedule/perform it? Merely giving the customer a tool to run, or instructing THEM to run it, does NOT count. Reply with exactly one JSON object and nothing else: {"claims_completion": true} or {"claims_completion": false}
